name: Ui_Window_SetMessageArg

Only caller 0x002ABE74 is still unnamed, so the caller side cannot add more.

name: maybe_Fs_ChannelTable_Create
summary: Constructor of the engine's fixed-capacity channel table: installs the two-vtable object header (0x007602B4 and 0x007602B4+0x18) over the inline storage returned by func_0010E8C0 and then constructs 0xFF entries of 0x18 bytes with entry constructor 0x00105570. name: maybe_Ui_Window_UpdateBackdrop

It also lazily builds the shared 0x1F-entry scratch table.

name: maybe_Ui_SoulWindow_Subwidget_Ctor

name: maybe_Ui_UpdateAllSlots

summary: Iterates slots 0..slot_count, fetches each slot object through vtable +0xE8, skips empty slots and sends refresh state 2 through vtable +0x128 to the slots that report 'needs refresh'. The Ghidra body is corrupt (unaff_ registers, halt_baddata), so the reading is asm-based.

Nothing named confirms the 'update all slots' reading.

name: maybe_Ui_Effect_Create
summary: Assigns the effect/resource selected by id to self+8: releases the old handle, lazily creates the 0x21C-byte pooled object (vtable 0x007829E0), resolves the id through Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple with a 0xC-byte descriptor and stores the new handle, releasing the temporary one.

name: Ui_UpdateInputState
summary: Applies the input lock for the current sub-window state (byte at self->f_728+0x14): all three states set the UI core's input flag through the context vtable, and states 1 and 2 additionally create the 0x1EB0-byte input object once and hand it to 0x001EE018.
evidence: The switch on the sub-window state byte, the repeated `(*(ctx->f_14+0x1c))+0xc` vtable call with argument 1 (an input enable/lock flag) in every branch, and the once-only 0x1EB0-byte object are all in the body; the object type itself is unnamed, so only the input-state part of the name is proven.

name: maybe_Ui_RowTable_InitFromRecord
summary: Builds the window's six-row descriptor table at self+0x49: fetches the record object through func_0063DD90, fills each 7-byte row (visible flag, colour index, colour word, text pointer), sets the pane texts and finally walks the row extents to compute the total size. The previous 'aspect object' reading does not match the body.
evidence: The body writes six 7-byte row records at self+0x49, each fed by maybe_Ui_SceneObjArray_Ctor's entry array (count at local_38, 0xC-byte entries with text pointers at +4), and then formats pane text with func_001A6680; that is a row table, not the aspect-ratio quad the old summary described. The record object (0xA24 bytes, vtable 0x00782990) is shared with other UI windows and is unnamed, which is why the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_CreateEntry
summary: Creates the 0x80-byte entry object for the dive form's current page, stores it in the slot at +0x210, starts it (0x00383A80 / 0x00644BE4) and pushes the resulting pane into the pane list at +0x134.
evidence: Ghidra's body is damaged (unaff_r4/r5/r8/r9, base pointer lost), but the surviving calls are the 0x80-byte pool allocation with constructor 0x00384050, the store to +0x210 and Ui_DiveForm_PushPane on self+0x134, matching the previous reading; the pane dimensions come from the still-unnamed table 0x0072C4C8.

name: maybe_Ui_TextLinePool_Init
summary: Window step handler (entry 0 of the step table at 0x00729398): rebuilds the shared pool of 0x1C-byte line records when the cached 'pool needed' flag is set, zeroes each record and installs its vtable, then reads the layout configuration and queues the next sub-state (6 or 0x0B) on the state vector at self+0x3B8.
evidence: Ghidra could not decompile this entry at all (the readable body is a single halt_baddata), so the reading is taken from the disassembly summarised in the header, including the step-table membership at 0x00729398 and the state pushes 6/0x0B. The +0x24A98 mentioned in the header is only the game-work pointer the singleton is read from - there is no Item_LookupRecord call and no item-id range in the function, so the checker's item-code flag does not apply. No named caller or callee confirms the pool role.

name: Ui_TextPage_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the text-page container: installs the vtable, initialises the two intrusive list heads (self+8/+0xC with sentinel self+0x14), sets up the small vector with inline storage at +0x6D4 and drains the free list. Called by the dive-form constructor.
evidence: The body is the classic container constructor shape (vtable store, list heads pointing at the inline sentinel, vector end pointer set to the inline buffer, free-list drain through 0x0070E0B0) and its caller 0x002FEE8C is the (maybe_)Ui_DiveForm_CtorB, which matches the previous evidence; the record layout itself is still unverified.

name: Ui_SetHitText
summary: Writes the hit/result counter into the pane named 'atari_txt7': looks the pane up through the layout vtable, walks the pane's child list, lazily creates the 0x98-byte text object with vtable 0x00782A08 and formats value with the "%d" format into that pane.

The window that owns the pane is unnamed, so the prefix 'Ui_' is as specific as the evidence allows.

name: Ui_BaseWindow_Release
summary: Shared release/destructor tail for base windows: calls the base teardown 0x0029F9E0, the class hook at vtable +0x4C, clears the per-object 'pool owner' flag at self+0x356C while clearing the shared pooled UI object, then runs the vtable +0x60 hook and rebinds the child pane.
evidence: It occupies the release slot of four window vtables (0x758C74, 0x75E6DC, 0x7627C8, 0x762DCC) and slot 5 of 0x768FC8, and the body calls the base teardown then only release hooks; the single ambiguous part is the 0x98-byte pooled object, which is a shared scratch object rather than a per-window allocation.

name: maybe_Map_RefreshLevelGrid
summary: Cached-revision refresh: compares self->f_31C with the revision counter at 0x007A36E4+8, and when they differ rebuilds the shared 0x98-byte UI object and forwards the new revision with 0x0017C9E4(object+0x9C, self->f_31C), then stores the revision.

name: maybe_Svc_SingletonCtor
summary: Lazy one-time construction of the engine's 0x37C-byte global UI/service singleton at g_007BE2F0 (vtable 0x00782928): zeroes the block, installs the vtable and returns the nested sub-object at +0x33C. The once flag is cleared after construction.

name: Ui_RegisterActor
signature: uint32_t Ui_RegisterActor(void* holder, void* actor, void* actorB, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Registers a pair of actors in a UI actor-slot holder: packs the two actor ids into holder+0xC/+0xD (0xFFFFF800 sentinel when an actor is missing), sets the initial delay 0xFFFFFFF, bumps the use counter at +0x10, binds the holder through the named Ui_ActorSlot_BindActor on the game work's +0x58 block and decrements the remaining-life counter at +0xF. Returns 1 on success.
evidence: The named callee Ui_ActorSlot_BindActor (0x00339FC0) is what makes the 'Ui actor slot registration' reading solid: this function is the code that fills the slot before binding it. The readable C is a damaged decompilation for one operand only (unaff_r7 in the sentinel expression); the disassembly at asm/text/text_00140048.s:67694-67720 shows it intact: `and r0,r7,r1` / `orr r0,r0,r1` with r1 = 0xFFFFF800, `strd r0,r1,[r4,#0x34]` with r1 = mvn #0xF0000000 (the 0x0FFFFFFF delay), the +0x40 use counter and the `subgt` life decrement at +0x3C, then `bl 0x339FC0`. The three callers (0x180B94, 0x1835AC, 0x184958) are still unnamed, so the owning window is not identified.

name: maybe_Ui_SetAnimFrame
summary: Fetches the widget's animation object through vtable +0x58 and applies the requested frame index packed with the widget's 16-bit layer id in the high half; does nothing when the widget has no animation object.
evidence: The body is exactly three operations (vtable +0x58 accessor, pack frame|layerId<<16, forward call), and six callers use it, but the callee it forwards to is currently named Ui_List_SelectEntryById (0x001D809C), which contradicts 'set animation frame' - the callee name is probably wrong for this use, so the frame interpretation cannot be fully confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_AbortOnIndexError
summary: Tail of an out-of-range table access: builds the shared 0x1C-byte helper, takes a timestamp, copies eight bytes out of it, calls maybe_Ui_ApplyCharacterLookParams(index) and then passes the result of the 0x00648B7C(self+0x11C, byte) lookup to the non-returning routine 0x00100B74.

name: maybe_Ui_List_ConfirmCurrent
summary: If the list widget has a current entry id at self+0x38, re-applies it through Ui_List_SelectEntryById (packing the u16 at +0x28 into the high half) and then calls the widget's vtable +0x3C notify slot with (self, 0, 0, 1).
evidence: Ui_List_SelectEntryById (0x001D809C) and the vtable +0x3C call with a trailing 1 are consistent with 'confirm the current entry', but the confirm notification itself is unnamed and no caller shows the answer being consumed.

name: maybe_Ui_Row_Activate
summary: Marks one of the row's three selection icons as current: clears the 'selected' bit (0xFE mask) on the first two child icons, sets it on the third, re-applies the row's entry id through Ui_List_SelectEntryById, then re-measures the text and re-applies the row.
evidence: The body's icon bit updates on the three child objects and the text re-apply are visible, but the function is Thumb with a damaged frame (unaff_r5/unaff_r11) and neither the row type nor the caller is named, so 'Activate' is still a description of the visible effect.

name: maybe_Actor2D_PlayAnimOnParts
summary: Three-state animation action for a 2D actor: state 0 waits out the duration at self->f_298+0x14, state 1 plays the shared anim id from func_00590504(1) on every actor in the two child lists (self+0x29C.. and self+0x2C0..), state 2 plays anim 2 on the second list, waits on the retarget timer and then restarts the clip. The previous 'factory that builds sprite panels' reading was wrong: there is no allocation and no table build, the body is a per-frame state machine.
evidence: The switch on self->f_2D4 with durations self->f_298->f_14/f_18/f_1C, the loop over the actor pointer lists calling the named Anim_PlayByIdForActor, and the absence of any allocation or mesh creation contradict the old 'BuildSpritePanelsFromRecord' name. Ghidra still reports bad instruction data in the middle of the function, so the exact part layout is uncertain.

name: Field_Object_PlayDefaultAnim
summary: Plays the object's default animation (the shared id from func_00590504(1)) and, depending on hide, either plays SE 0xA4 through the lazily created 0x1EB0-byte sound manager or snaps the animator to its last frame and tells the object (vtable +0x40) to enter state 4; finally sets state 4 through vtable +0x58 and clears self[0xA2].
evidence: The named Anim_PlayByIdForActor / Sound_PlaySeById calls and the vtable state changes match the previous reading, and the function is called from three field-object paths; only the flag at self[0xA2] is still unexplained.

name: Monster_ActionScaleGrow
summary: Three-state monster action that grows a monster: waits for the actor to be ready, plays the shared grow animation, waits for the clip to end, then each frame adds 1.0 to the Y-scale of the action's actor (self->f_30) and its companion (self->f_28) and advances both animator frames until the clip's frame count is reached; then plays the idle animation and finishes.
evidence: The body is exactly this ladder (vtable +0x34 readiness check, Anim_PlayByIdForActor, func_00669B98 clip query, the 0x3F800000 increment on f_9C of both actors, frame writes at +0x12A and the final Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState); the vtable 0x0076AEBC is one of the monster action-behaviour tables.

name: maybe_Gfx_Effect_Update
summary: Per-frame state update for a 2D field/sprite actor: refreshes the model record, returns while the 'active' byte at +0x29B is clear, switches to state 4 through vtable +0x40 when the byte at +0x29D is set, and otherwise plays the actor's configured animation (id from 0x00725B08) and snaps its animator to the last frame.
evidence: The body is a small state dispatch over the two flag bytes, but which object class it belongs to is unclear - it is not obviously an effect (the only named helpers are the generic Anim_PlayByIdForActor and maybe_Field_SceneObject_SetAnimatorLastFrame), so the 'Gfx_Effect' prefix may be wrong.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_StopAnimAndHide
summary: Stops a sprite actor: plays its stop animation (id at 0x00727940, mode 1), tells the object to enter state 4 through vtable +0x3C and sets the hidden byte f_7D.
evidence: The three-step body matches the name exactly and the only caller is the (maybe_)Gfx_SpriteActor_StopAttachedEffect path; mode 1 on Anim_PlayByIdForActor is the stop/finish mode used by the other stop helpers.

name: maybe_Actor_StopAttachedEffect
summary: If the owning actor (component-0x22C) is currently visible, plays the stop animation 0x002F2F08 on it, snaps its animator to the last frame, sets state 4 through vtable +0x58 and clears the component's +0x5C/+0xAC counters.
evidence: The owner-offset arithmetic and the four cleanup steps are clear, but the animation call uses mode 0 rather than a stop mode and 0x002F2F08 is an unnamed animation id, so what is actually attached/detached remains a guess.

name: maybe_Monster_FieldBehaviour_UpdatePhysics
summary: Large movement/physics step for the field-monster behaviours: reads the camera/party input flags through maybe_Party_MemberFlagPairA/B, integrates the turn and bob rates from the behaviour's float fields, builds the orientation matrix with the vector/quaternion helpers, commits the actor position and pushes a trail sample.
evidence: The body's float integration and the vector helpers (0x005754C0/0x005755C8/0x005F5F54) are visible, but it also reads the UI overlay manager through work+0x48 (func_006343CC), which is unusual for monster physics, and the two callers 0x003AF004/0x003AF284 are unnamed; the 'physics' reading is still an interpretation.

name: Ui3D_ComputeOrientationBasis
summary: Builds the orientation basis for a 3D UI element from the rotation stored at host+0x88..0xA4, optionally folding in the world matrix of the scene node named "N_ALL", fixes the handedness when the trace is negative, normalises the axes and applies the resulting basis to the draw object at self+0x50.
evidence: The quaternion-to-basis arithmetic, the two Math_MatrixMultiply calls, the "N_ALL" node lookup through 0x00633C38 and the final application through func_0058E594 are all present; the node name and the sign-fix branch make the orientation-basis reading solid, while the host class itself stays unnamed (hence the generic Ui3D prefix).

name: Ui_ListWindow_UpdateRowText
summary: Refreshes one battle list row: compares the row's cached ids against self+0x50..0x5E, switches on the row kind (0..8) to fetch the primary and secondary strings from the text table, enables the second column and, for actor rows, resolves the party member record through func_0035EB98 or the battle unit lists at +0x4254/+0x428C to pick the icon.
evidence: The named callees Ui_TextElement_SetString, Ui_TextTable_GetStringById, Ui_TextElement_SetSecondColumn and Ui_SpriteSpan_Select plus the party-member lookup func_0035EB98 pin down a row-text refresh. The readable C is a damaged decompilation (cr_ registers, a fake software_udf at the not-found branch), but the disassembly at asm/text/text_00400048.s:64929-64990 is clean: it loads the member id with `ldrb r4,[r1,#0x768]`, calls 0x0035EB98, compares the cached ids at self+0x5E/0x50/0x54/0x5C/0x58 against row+0xE8/0xFC/0x100/0xF5/0x104 and then switches on the signed kind byte row+0xFC with a jump table for 0..9. The row structure itself is still unnamed.

name: Ui_ListWindow_UpdateSecondaryText
summary: Helper of the battle row update: returns when the row has no secondary id, sets the primary string and clears the second column, then for member/monster rows resolves the actor or sprite from the battle unit lists (+0x4254/+0x428C) and selects the icon, or falls back to the text-table entry 7.
evidence: Same named callee set as the main row updater (Ui_TextElement_SetString/SetSecondColumn, Ui_SpriteSpan_Select, func_0035EB98) and it operates on the same row offsets (+0xD/+0xE kind bytes, +0x100/+0x104 ids), which is why the two are now named as a pair; which of the two gets called for which row kind is still only partly clear.

name: Os_WorkQueue_Push
signature: u32 Os_WorkQueue_Push(WorkQueue* q, int wait, u32 arg3, int* node)
summary: Publishes the next work item on a queue: reserves a free node, and while none is free drains the completion queue (folding the finished item id into q->f_178/f_188), links the node at the tail, then either tries a non-blocking push or waits on the queue's send primitive; returns the sequence number or 0.
evidence: The body is built from the named Os_QueueTryPop/Os_QueueTryPush primitives, keeps an explicit head/tail pair (f_16C/f_170) and a sequence counter (f_174), and has seven callers including the sound-stream submit paths - that is a producer side of a queue, so 'Push' is descriptive rather than speculative.

name: maybe_Snd_ShutdownEngine
signature: void maybe_Snd_ShutdownEngine(void* engine, u32 arg2, u32* mask, int count)
summary: Stops the sound engine: marks f_358/f_348, waits on and closes the session handle at f_344, releases the command buffer at f_340, then walks a caller-supplied bitmask and for each set bit releases the 0x1C-byte voice record at f_24 + i*0x1C, closing its stream when requested.
evidence: The callees (0x0010DF40/0x0010DF90, Snd_ReleaseAllChannels) and the bitmask loop over 0x1C-byte voice records fit 'release these voices', but Ghidra lost several registers (unaff_r5/r6/r8/r11), the function is Thumb with overlapping instructions, and whether it is the whole-engine shutdown or only a per-call release is unclear.

name: Os_WorkQueue_Drain
summary: Discards every pending completion of a work queue: pops each finished node with Os_QueueTryPop, stores its item id in q->f_178, walks to the tail of the node chain and records the last in-flight id, clearing it when it matches q->f_184.
evidence: The body is the same completion-folding block that Os_WorkQueue_Push runs while waiting for a free node (identical code at 0x00114E60), now as a stand-alone loop built on the named Os_QueueTryPop; one caller is Sound_StreamThread_Main, i.e. a queue-owner thread draining before shutdown.

name: maybe_Gfx_UploadQueuedTextures
signature: void maybe_Gfx_UploadQueuedTextures(void* self, u32 arg2, int count)
summary: Services a batch of pending transfer records under the shared mutex: walks the bitmask at self+0x2C, and for every set bit with a live entry at self+0x24 + i*0x1C handles its stream/object, marks it done and bumps the completed counter at +0x70.
evidence: Its only caller is maybe_Gfx_UpdateFrameTasks (0x0010293C), which services the pending-transfer list, and the mutex/counter handling fits a queue servicer; however the per-entry work is the same 0x1C-byte record loop that the sound release path (0x00108F32) uses, so whether these records are textures, streams or voices - and thus the 'UploadQueuedTextures' wording - is not proven.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateActionSequence
summary: Continuation of the battle action-sequence state machine: the state at self[0x4D] starts at 0xB7B, scans the four battle unit lists (+0x428C) for the first non-empty one, picks a random unit through the battle RNG, sets the primary target self[0x51] and drives the target/hit stages, finally moving the unit's secondary state machine (+0x14) to 5/6/7.
evidence: The body is the same state machine as maybe_Battle_StartActionSequence (0x00173CD0) without its opening effect reset, and uses the documented battle offsets (RNG +0x4218, unit lists +0x428C, flag +0x4244); the sibling 0x00173CD0 is still a maybe_, so calling this the 'update' half is descriptive rather than proven.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateModel
summary: Per-frame model update for a field actor: resolves its object handle by type (0x001C8EDC), runs the actor's vtable +0xD0 step, switches on the model's kind (0x212/0x215/0xAB...) to apply the ground/effect offset, then updates the animation transform and the collision position.
evidence: The body is a model/transform update (handle resolve, vtable +0xD0, per-kind offsets, collision position), but several of its helpers are still unnamed (0x0030A0E0/0x0030AC50/0x002E7F08) and one named callee in the same path is Ui_Span_IsIdle, so the exact split between model and collision work is unverified.

name: maybe_Field_NpcUpdateFacing
signature: void maybe_Field_NpcUpdateFacing(NpcBehavior* self, int mode, uint32_t arg3)
summary: Updates the actor's turn/facing flags for the given mode: reads the world's 2D/3D mode (work+0x3C values 1 and 4) and the extra flag at +0x44, sets or clears the two direction bytes f_36/f_37 of the actor at self+0x60, then forwards the command to the scene-node children.
evidence: The world-mode switches and the direction-flag writes are clear, and the tail call is the named Field_SceneNode_ForwardCommandToChildren, but the two bytes f_36/f_37 are not proven to be facing (they could be visibility/animation flags), so the 'facing' part remains a guess.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_SpawnEffectInstance
summary: Initialises a field model actor and spawns its attached effect: notifies the scene-node children, sets the marker byte at +0x15C, selects entry 0 of the keyed list at +0x60 and, when the enable byte +0x3AA is set, builds a position/rotation parameter block and calls Effect_FindOrCreateInstance on the effect manager (work+0x60) with effect id 0x4AD, storing it at +0x314.
evidence: The named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and Container_KeyedList_SelectEntry calls plus the field-scene-node update rule out a UI window (the previous 'Ui_Window' prefix was wrong); the effect id 0x4AD and the parameter block are concrete, but which visual effect 0x4AD is stays unknown.

name: maybe_Field_Prop_Destruct
summary: Two-instruction teardown: runs the shared scene-node cleanup 0x005E7594 and then reselects entry 0 of the keyed list at self+0x60. The identical body exists at 0x003E60F0.
evidence: The body is byte-identical to 0x003E60F0 (which the first pass called maybe_Field_Actor_StopActionObj), so only one of the two names can be right and neither is proven; 0x005E7594 is unnamed and Container_KeyedList_SelectEntry is a list operation, not a release.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_StopActionObj
summary: Two-instruction teardown: runs the shared scene-node cleanup 0x005E7594 and then reselects entry 0 of the keyed list at self+0x60. The identical body exists at 0x002FB644.
evidence: Same body as 0x002FB644 (the two were given conflicting names in the first pass), and the only calls are an unnamed cleanup plus a list selection, so neither 'prop destructor' nor 'stop action object' is established.

name: Ui_Part_ConfirmWithSe1
summary: Confirm wrapper used by the skill-panel handlers: when the part has not been initialised yet (f_14 == 0) and the argument is non-zero it lazily creates the sound work and plays SE 1, then always tail-calls the shared handler 0x0029126C(self, arg2).

name: maybe_PartyPanel_UpdateHighlight
summary: Updates one item/party panel: advances its animation state, and when the state is 0x28 plays SE 5 or starts cue 0x39 depending on the flag at f_230; then, when the panel's item id changes, looks the item up through Item_LookupRecord / func_0066B2CC and refreshes the payout gauge and the icon.
evidence: The item lookup, the 0x1E price/gauge setup and the Ids at f_240/f_244 show this is a shop/party item panel update rather than a plain 'highlight', so the old name is too narrow; the panel class itself is unnamed, which is why the guess stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Menu_AttachActorToWindow
signature: int maybe_Menu_AttachActorToWindow(MenuState* self, int column, unsigned slot, unsigned entry, unsigned flags, int immediate)
summary: Attaches the actor for a battle-menu entry to the actor slot of the given column: picks the battle or field list base by the battle flag at work+0x4244, resolves the unit through func_002AB62C(self+0x428C+column*0x1C, slot), rejects when the party already has 8 active members, sets the unit's state through vtable +0x44 and then either links it with func_00606AE8 or issues SE 0x27 when 'immediate' is set.
evidence: The battle-work offsets (+0x4244 flag, +0x428C lists), the named Party_CountActive and the vtable +0x44 state call are concrete, but the attach helpers 0x00606AE8/0x00601CC0 are unnamed and 'to window' is only inferred from the calling menu.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleTargetMove
summary: Target-selection movement step: when the input mask at self+0x4C has the movement bits and the cursor is enabled, plays the move SE, recomputes the screen positions (f_E4/f_E8) of the selected party member and its actor slot, then refreshes the command widget through its +0x50 virtual.
evidence: The input-mask gate, the named Sound_PlaySeById / Ui_PartyStatusWindow_GetSelectedMemberId / Ui_Widget_CountChildren calls and the member record updates are visible, but the 'target move' reading depends on what the +0x4C bits mean and the enclosing battle-command window is unnamed.

name: Field_Gadget_TriggerCommand10
signature: int Field_Gadget_TriggerCommand10(FieldObject* self, uint32_t arg2, uint32_t arg3, uint32_t arg4)
summary: Triggers the field gadget command for this object: plays SE 9, issues gadget command 10 with the object's id through the named Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand on the event state (work+0x6C), and on success resets the object's animation; on failure clears the busy flag f_2A3.
evidence: The named callee Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand with literal command 10 is decisive for the command part; the old name said 'TriggerEffect', but the body issues a gadget command and only plays a sound - no effect instance is created (the 'effect' wording came from the wrong assumption that 0x001EBC68 is an effect helper).

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_UpdateDrawPos
summary: Recomputes a 2D sprite's screen rectangle: takes the sprite size from its model record, divides by 8, adds the actor's +0x78/+0x7C draw offset, builds the transform through 0x0031A658 and, when the debug flag +0x29D or 0x00669B98 allows it, submits the rectangle for drawing.
evidence: The size/8 arithmetic, the two 0x0031A658 transform calls and the clipping bounds are all in the body, which makes 'update draw position' accurate; whether the object is a sprite actor (rather than a 2D field object) is still inferred from the caller, and the submit helpers 0x00251230/0x0022D5C4 are unnamed.

name: Ui_JackpotScreen_EndPayout
summary: Ends a casino jackpot payout: clears the payout counters, plays SE 0xEA8, applies the payout amount from 0x0063C2F4 to the wallet at work+0x24A98, resets the slot-machine reel widgets and the pane animation references, then restores the start position from the layout table 0x0072AA0C.
evidence: The body combines the named Sound_PlaySeById, the coin counter helper func_0061251C on the bag/work block (+0x24A98), and Ui_SlotMachine_PlayStartAnim on the payout widget - a slot-machine payout end, which matches the name; the 'jackpot' wording comes from the slot machine, not from a proven screen class.

name: Sound_PlaySeFromTable
signature: u8 Sound_PlaySeFromTable(void* self, u32 handle, int tableIndex, int direction, u32 category, u32 argument)
summary: Table-driven sound-effect player: indexes the 4-byte entry table hanging off the data manager record (GameWork+0x28C, count at record+0x60), rejects out-of-range indexes and entries with no sound id, derives the volume/pan from the direction (self+0x1AB4..0x1AC0) and the category bitmask g_001EC98C, and plays the result through the shared sound player.
evidence: The bounds checks against the table count, the direction-to-volume arithmetic with the named sound player call and the four volume constants at 0x001EC980..0x001EC988 make the role clear; one caller is 0x005E9B6C (field SE dispatch), and the function returns 0 on every rejection path as a 'did not play' flag.

name: maybe_FieldParty_PlayMemberVoiceById
signature: int maybe_FieldParty_PlayMemberVoiceById(void* group, void* actor, int slot)
summary: Plays one of two sound ids for a party member: resolves the member record from the actor's character id (func_0035EB98), reads the equipped item for the given slot (func_006292F0), and when that item exists plays the sound id stored in its data-manager row (f_be), otherwise falls back to the group's current member row (f_aa). Returns 0 when nothing is played.
evidence: The named callees (func_0035EB98 member record, func_006292F0 equipped item, Item_LookupRecord, Sound_PlaySeById) prove an item/record-driven sound choice, but calling the ids 'voice' is an interpretation: the ids live in item/monster data rows, not in a voice table, and the only reference is the group's own vtable.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandSelect
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandSelect(int* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Battle command-window select step: refreshes the member widget (vtable +0x70) and the window, and when the confirm bit is set checks Battle_Item_CanTargetActor, builds the command for the highlighted slot (byte at self+0x40A+slot*8) with maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_ConstructCommands, advances the command script to 0x12 and plays the confirm SE; the cancel bit forwards the stored command id and refreshes the widget.
evidence: The named Battle_Item_CanTargetActor / maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_ConstructCommands calls and the script state 0x12 are concrete, but the three sibling handlers (0x0027E8CC, 0x0027FC60, 0x00280210) share the same input guard and differ only in which command id they push, so which one is 'select' versus 'confirm' is still partly guesswork.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleSecondaryInput
summary: Second input branch of the battle command window: on the confirm bit it plays SE 0 and constructs the 4 by 8-byte command array with the 0xFF 'none' marker; on the cancel bit it runs the no-op step, refreshes the widget and pushes command id 0x10 into the command script.
evidence: Nothing in the body supports the previous 'debug combo' name: it is the same input-guard pattern as its two neighbours with command id 0x10 and a 4x8 command array. The real distinction between the three siblings is not visible without the (unnamed) surrounding window, so the name is deliberately vague.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandConfirm
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCommandConfirm(int* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Confirm branch of the battle command window: when the confirm bit is set it sends the selected member id to the state machine, reads the highlighted command id through vtable +0x44 and, unless it is 0x1A (the 'back' entry), pushes it into the command script and plays the confirm SE; the cancel bit pushes command 0xB and refreshes the widget.
evidence: The 0x1A special case plus the command-id forwarding explain the two branches, and the named Ui_PartyStatusWindow_GetSelectedMemberId anchors it in the command window, but as with its siblings no caller identifies which menu stage actually invokes it.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitDisplay
summary: Per-frame battle display update: returns immediately once the finished flags +0xD2/+0xD3 are set, otherwise polls all units through vtable +0x48 for the 'busy' byte f_108, then runs the stage state machine at self[0x497] that advances unit animations, spawns damage popups and waits for the camp/menu fade.
evidence: The unit enumeration (vtable +0x48, count 0x00630DC8) and the busy-byte polling are clear, and the body contains the named maybe_Battle_PopupEntry_Create / Sound_PlaySeById calls, but the 0x497 stage switch covers much more than 'unit display' (camp fade, popups), so the name is narrower than the function.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateTurn
summary: Per-turn body of the battle action sequence: runs the turn state machine (0x1688 / 0x1697 / 0x16A6 / 0x16DE ...), waits for all units to be ready, advances the party/member cursor state machines and the action text, and moves to the next turn state. Returns 1 once the finished byte +0xD2 is set.
evidence: The large state ladder and the many party/target helpers (0x001FB4A4, 0x001FE804, 0x001FD2CC, 0x003C3074, 0x00429BD8) are visible, but nearly all of them are unnamed and the state numbers (0x1688..0x16DE) are not documented anywhere, so 'update turn' is a description of the neighbourhood rather than proven stage semantics.

name: Ui_MessagePart_UpdateAll
summary: Updates the message window's 0x60 text-part slots: for each 0x18-byte record whose id matches the current sequence number it fires the record's callback/sprite update, rebuilds the four active-part ids at +0xA84 and frees the stale sprite handles.
evidence: The fixed 0x60-slot loop over 0x18-byte records with the callback at +0x184 and sprite handle at +0x18C, plus the adjacent message-part helpers (0x003E15D8 text clamp, 0x003E1A28 AddGlyphPart), make the message-part pool reading solid; the callback targets themselves are unnamed.

name: Ui_Fade_UpdateWithSe
summary: Frame-based fade step with cubic easing: advances the frame counter, interpolates the target's vertical offset (f_144) over the first 16 frames, plays SE 0x2E on frame 0x14, resets the attached animation refs at frames 0x14 and 0x1B and reports completion after frame 0x38.
evidence: The frame checkpoints (0x10/0x14/0x1B/0x38), the cubic easing constants and the literal SE id 0x2E are all in the body, and the target write is the same +0x1C offset the fade helpers use; only the owning screen class is unnamed.

name: Monster_FieldBehaviour_PlayRunEffect
summary: Run presentation of a field-monster behaviour: resets the actor's animation, switches it to the "Run" animation, records the linked model id in the behaviour, spawns the configured effect in front of the actor through Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and plays SE 0xFC.
evidence: The literal "Run" name pointer at 0x003AEEF0 passed to the actor's animation vtable +0x84, the effect id passed to the named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and Sound_PlaySeById(0xFC) are all explicit; slot 2 of the same behaviour vtable (0x003AF504) confirms the monster-behaviour family.

name: Battle_Ui_PlayMemberSound
signature: void Battle_Ui_PlayMemberSound(void* self, int state, PartyMember* member, u32 seId, int argument)
summary: Plays the sound that belongs to a party member's battle state: maps the state codes (-1, 0, -3, -4, -5, -9, -0xB, -0x11, -0x19, -0x1A) to a small set of SE ids (0x129, 0x12A, 0x158 ...) and plays them, with a separate branch when the battle flag at work+0x4244 is set.
evidence: The state-to-SE ladder is entirely visible and every branch ends in the named Sound_PlaySeById; the seId lookup func_0063E60C on the data manager is used for the 'voice' variant, which is why 'member sound' (not 'menu SE') is the safe wording.

name: Battle_Ui_PlaySeForEvent
summary: Plays the sound for a battle UI event: events -4/-0x19 play the id 0x12A+7, events -5/-0x1A play the same id but return whether it actually started, and every other event plays 0x12A; when the battle flag work+0x4244 is set some events are suppressed.
evidence: The event switch on the short at event+4 and the three distinct SE paths are explicit, and the return value is the sound player's result; the exact meaning of the event codes is still unknown but the 'play SE for event' role is not.

name: Actor_UpdateStateSeTimerA
summary: Advances an actor's state sound timer: clears the state byte f_2EC when the scene's attract/auto flags are set, and while the state is 1 or 2 decrements the integer timer at f_2F0 and plays a sound effect once it reaches zero.
evidence: The attract-flag check on work+0x44/+0x45, the integer decrement of f_2F0 and the single Sound_PlaySeById call are all in the body, and its twin 0x0022C8AC does the same with a float timer at +4.

name: Actor_UpdateStateSeTimerB
summary: Float-timer twin of 0x0022C884: same attract-flag check, but the timer is the float at state+4; while the state byte is 1 or 2 it subtracts the frame delta and plays the same sound effect when the timer reaches zero.
evidence: Identical struct offsets and globals as 0x0022C884 with the float subtraction `*(float*)(state+4) - dt`; the pair is clearly the integer/float instantiations of one timer helper.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ResetSelection
signature: void maybe_Ui_BattleCommandWindow_ResetSelection(BattleWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: On a fresh confirm input (self->f_130 & 0x102) it refreshes the member widget (vtable +0x70), reads the highlighted command id through vtable +0x44 and, unless it is the 0x1A 'back' entry, pushes it into the command script and plays the confirm SE.
evidence: The body forwards the selected command id into the script, which is the opposite of 'reset the selection' - the name is probably wrong, but the correct verb (confirm vs execute) cannot be decided without the window's other handlers (0x0027E8CC/0x0027FC60/0x00280210 all look similar).

name: Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancelB
signature: u32 Ui_BattleCmd_HandleCancelB(int* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Cancel branch of the battle command window: on a cancel input it optionally plays the cancel SE, calls the window's own cancel slot (+0x4C with 0,1) and resets the command script to step 0.
evidence: The call to the object's own vtable +0x4C with (0,1) and the reset of the command script via the +0x14 virtual to 0 are exactly a cancel/back action, and the input mask gate (0x106) matches the other cancel paths in this window.

name: maybe_Ui_PlaySeForAnimState
summary: Two-step helper: selects the next pane group through 0x0039921C (currently named Ui_CreditWindow_SelectPaneGroup) and plays SE 0xE56.
evidence: The 64-byte body contains only the group-select call and Sound_PlaySeById(0xE56); nothing ties it to an 'animation state', so the previous name over-specifies. Only the literal SE id is concrete.

name: Ui_CreditWindow_PlayShakeAndSe
summary: Plays a credit-window pane animation clamped to id 3 at self+0x3F8, resets the shake state at self+0x9C and plays SE 0xE50.
evidence: The clamp `animId > 3 ? 3 : animId`, the named Ui_CreditWindow_PlayPaneAnim and Ui_AnimShake_Update calls plus the literal SE 0xE50 are all present, so both halves of the name are justified.

name: maybe_Ui_PlayConfirmSeIfFlagged
signature: void maybe_Ui_PlayConfirmSeIfFlagged(UiWidget* self, int arg2, int b, void* ctxOut)
summary: Plays SE 9 when the widget's flag byte at +0x296 is set; otherwise does nothing. Twin of 0x0028EBE4 which tests the byte at +0x2C7.
evidence: The single conditional plus Sound_PlaySeById(9) is unambiguous, and the twin at 0x0028EBE4 differs only in the flag offset, but that SE 9 means 'confirm' is an assumption from the UI family, not from the body or a named caller (0x0044CE00 is unnamed).

name: maybe_Ui_PlayConfirmSeIfFlaggedB
signature: void maybe_Ui_PlayConfirmSeIfFlaggedB(UiWidget* self, int arg2, int b, void* ctxOut)
summary: Plays SE 9 when the widget's flag byte at +0x2C7 is set; otherwise does nothing. Twin of 0x0028E46C which tests the byte at +0x296.
evidence: Same body as 0x0028E46C with the other flag offset; the confirm interpretation is still inherited from the first pass rather than proven by a named caller (0x0044D1B0 is unnamed).

name: maybe_Field_Object_UpdateSeState
summary: Starts or stops the object's looping SE depending on its linked record: when the record's first u16 is 0x9DB it (re)starts SE 4, otherwise it plays SE 4 only when the animation id differs from the stored one; then stores the state byte f_2BA and forwards the command to the scene-node children.
evidence: The data-manager record compare against 0x9DB and the two Sound_PlaySeById(4, ...) calls with opposite loop flags are visible, but the Thumb body has damaged registers (unaff_r4/r6/r7/r9, in_ZR), so which object field drives the decision is only partly readable.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_PlayStepSounds
signature: void maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_PlayStepSounds(BattleSequence* self, u32 first, u32 last)
summary: Builds and dispatches the action message for entries first..last: walks the 0x68-byte action entries at self+0xBAB0, accumulates the message words, plays the action's sound id (record +0x2CE) and finally calls the sequence's vtable +0xF4 with the accumulated message.
evidence: The loop over 0x68-byte entries, the accumulator at local_30 and the vtable +0xF4 dispatch are visible, and the only SE call uses the entry's sound id, but the 'step sounds' wording is inherited from the first pass - the function's main output is the message passed to +0xF4, so it does more than play step sounds.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_HandleTextInput
signature: void maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_HandleTextInput(void* self, u16* charPtr, u32 glyphSource, int flag)
summary: Character-input helper: resolves the font record for the typed character and, when there is none, forwards the raw code with a default glyph; the rest of the function is lost to Ghidra (bad instruction data at the second half).
evidence: Only the first branch is readable (font lookup 0x0061BD4C and the glyph helpers on self+0x198); the function is truncated by halt_baddata, so both the 'equipment window' owner and the text-edit behaviour are unverified.

name: Ui_Smith_UpdateHitEffect
summary: Frame timer of the blacksmith mini-game: plays the hammer SE 0xEE8 on frame 2, spawns the spark effect (id from the table at 0x003B7090) at the anvil on frame 0x2D and plays its SE, and after frame 0x40 copies the two result words from the mini-game descriptor into the result object.
evidence: The frame checkpoints 2/0x2D/0x40, the two literal SE ids, the named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance call and the result copies from 0x003B709C are all explicit; the 'Smith' identity comes from the sibling animation table ("SmithStart") in the same block.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_PlaySeA
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_PlaySeA(void* self, BattleActor* actor, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Plays a member widget's sound: first the actor's own animation SE (actor+0xB8), then either 0x158 or 0x15D depending on the member flag at +0x10, unless the battle flag work+0x4244 redirects to the widget's vtable +0x138.
evidence: Both SE paths are visible, but the Thumb body is damaged (unaff_r5/r6/r9, `*(u32*)(unaff_r9 + self)` for the sound player) and the widget class is unnamed, so 'MemberWidget' and the A/B suffix only reflect this function's place in the vtable family.

name: Sound_PlaySeId9
summary: Lazily creates the shared 0x1EB0-byte sound manager on first use and then plays sound effect id 9 on every call.
evidence: The body is the same lazy-init block used everywhere the sound manager is needed, followed by one Sound_PlaySeById(id 9); the previous name said 'Once', which is wrong - only the manager creation happens once, the effect is played on every call. It is the fixed-id twin of 0x001E3C74.

name: Sound_PlaySeWithWorkInit
summary: Generic SE-once-with-lazy-manager helper: creates the shared 0x1EB0-byte sound manager when the caller's once flag is set and then plays seId through it.
evidence: Identical body to 0x00181848 except that the effect id is the second argument, and both use the same once-flag + pool block and vtable 0x00782914 that every other SE call site in this batch uses for the sound manager; no named caller exists, so it is reached through a bound/vtable reference.

name: maybe_FieldParty_SelectMemberVoiceId
signature: unsigned maybe_FieldParty_SelectMemberVoiceId(void* work, Actor* actor, ActorParam* param, int force)
summary: Chooses and plays the sound id for an actor from its category code: -0x13/-0x14 play 0x15C, -4/-0x19 play 0x131, -5/-0x1A play 0x132, -0x12 is silent and everything else plays 0x129/0x12A depending on whether the actor is a party member; the positive categories branch on the param byte +0x26 and on force.
evidence: The category ladder and the direct Sound_PlaySeById calls are clear (they do not go through a voice table), so 'VoiceId' is an interpretation - the ids are plain SE/character sound ids. The positive-category branch calls maybe_Text_Row_IsMonsterType, which hints at monster-versus-party barks rather than a voice bank.

name: maybe_FieldParty_SelectMemberVoiceById
signature: void maybe_FieldParty_SelectMemberVoiceById(unsigned arg1, Actor* actor, ActorParam* param, int force)
summary: Second variant of the member sound selector: chooses 0x15C / 0x15A / 0x15D for the character categories, and when not forced reads the sound id from the character record (u16 at +200) fetched by the actor's character id; always ends by playing the chosen id.
evidence: The character-record lookup func_0063E5C8(actor->f_768) with the u16 at +200 is a concrete data source, but the constants 0x15A/0x15C/0x15D are not proven to be voice ids and the 'ById' suffix in the name adds nothing the body shows.

name: maybe_FieldParty_PlayCommonVoice
summary: Three-instruction sound request: gets the shared sound player and plays SE 300 with no arguments.
evidence: The body is only Sound_GetPlayer + Sound_PlaySeById(300), so what makes 300 a 'common voice' (as opposed to any other SE) cannot be seen here; it is self-referenced through a 9-entry vtable, which is why no caller is available to clarify.

name: Ui_Part_ConfirmWithSe1B
summary: Second instantiation of the skill-panel confirm wrapper (compile-time copy of 0x0018FD04 with other globals): when the part is not yet initialised and the argument is non-zero it lazily creates the sound manager and plays SE 1, then tail-calls the shared handler 0x0029126C(self, arg2).
evidence: Byte-identical body to the just-confirmed Ui_Part_ConfirmWithSe1 (0x0018FD04) apart from the singleton globals, and its caller 0x0037B224 is in the same skill-panel family; the B suffix correctly marks it as the second template instantiation.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_PlaySe50WhenThrottled
summary: Timed-part update hook: forwards to the child object (vtable +0x2C) and, while the part's latch f_1C4 is set, the timer predicate 0x00649BFC is true and the threshold f_18C exceeds 8.0, plays SE 0x32 (=50) once and clears the latch.
evidence: The literal 0x32 and the 8.0 float threshold (0x41200000) are visible and the play-once latch is clear, but nothing proves the 8.0 value is a 'throttle'; the name keeps that interpretation from the first pass.

name: Ui_Cue_Update
summary: Per-frame tick of a UI cue: adds 1/30 s to the float timer at +0x14 and, once the duration at +0xC is reached, plays the cue's sound id (first word), stores the returned handle at +8 and loads the next callback pair from the descriptor at 0x0072A79C (+0x70/+0x74).
evidence: The 1/30 second step (0x3D088889), the duration comparison, the Sound_PlaySeById with the cue's own id and the two-word descriptor reload are all explicit, and the neighbouring cue helpers (Ui_Cue_Start in maybe_PartyPanel_UpdateHighlight) use the same object.

name: Sound_PlaySe52or53
summary: Plays SE 0x53 or 0x52 depending on the flag byte at part->f_28+0x3C4, after lazily creating the shared sound manager.
evidence: Both literal ids and the flag branch are explicit and the lazy-manager block is the standard one; the name is deliberately literal because the flag's meaning is unknown.

name: Ui_JackpotScreen_EndSequence
summary: Closes the slot-machine/jackpot sequence: if the payout widget's animation has finished, plays SE 0xEA7 and resets the roulette panels; then invokes the screen's next callback and restores the start position from the layout table 0x0072AA0C.
evidence: The named maybe_Ui_RouletteWindow_ResetPanels / maybe_Ui_Screen_InvokeNextCallback calls, the SE id 0xEA7 and the same layout-table restore as the confirmed Ui_JackpotScreen_EndPayout (0x002C7B58) make the jackpot-screen reading consistent.

name: Model_PlaySeOnFlag
summary: Plays SE 0x12E when the attached model exists and its flag f_6FD is set, after running the model's attach/fade step.
evidence: The body is a single guarded SE play (model pointer +0x160 node check, flag f_6FD, literal SE 0x12E) and the named model helpers 0x005E7848/maybe_Model_Attach_SetFadeRange frame it, so the name is a literal description of the code.

name: Actor_MoveToPointAndPlaySe
summary: Moves a field actor toward a target point: plays SE 0xFD once (latched by f_40), computes the XY offset to the target position from the model node, interpolates the actor's f_38/f_3C and, once within the 1.0 distance threshold, applies the position and starts the arrival animation.
evidence: The one-shot SE latch, the 0.5 interpolation factor, the 1.0 arrival threshold and the position apply / animation start calls are all in the body; the class is unnamed but its fields and behaviour match the field actor mover family.

name: Field_TimerPlaySe254
summary: Frame counter for a field timer: increments the counter at timer+0x34 and, when it catches the limit at timer+0x30, plays SE 0xFE and resets limit=4, counter=0. Returns the timer pointer so it can be chained.
evidence: The counter/limit pair, the literal SE 0xFE and the reset to 4/0 are all explicit; its caller is the (maybe_)Field_Actor_CheckCellTransition, which fits a timer consulted at cell boundaries.

name: Sound_PlaySeIfBelow
summary: Plays seId through the lazily created sound manager, but only when limit is greater than seId (an early return otherwise).
evidence: The whole body is the `limit <= seId -> return` guard plus the standard lazy-manager SE call, so the name states exactly what the code does; what the limit represents is left to the (unnamed) callers.

name: Ui_Timer_CountdownSe221
summary: Timed UI part tick: forwards to the child object, then while the counter f_140 is positive decrements it and plays SE 0xDD when it reaches zero; when bit 0x10 of f_138 is set it instead resets the part (f_13D=0, f_94=0, f_140=1).
evidence: The countdown, the literal SE 0xDD and the reset branch are explicit in the body; the part object is the same shared UI part used by the other 0x98-byte UI objects.

name: maybe_Field_ActorActionSeq_ApplyActorCommand
summary: Applies the current per-actor command of a field action sequence: for an 'M'-type entry it takes the actor through vtable +0x4C, adds the action state flags (maybe_Battle_AddStateFlags) and releases the pending action object, then bumps the actor index, wraps it at the sequence's actor count and applies the animation and SE for the new actor.
evidence: The 'M' type test, the named maybe_Battle_AddStateFlags call and the actor-index wrap around func_00630D64 are visible, but the function combines two jobs (apply command + advance actor) and the name only describes the first; the second half (vtable +0xCC and the SE id at +0x16BA) is still unclear.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberAnim_PlaySeB
signature: void Battle_Ui_MemberAnim_PlaySeB(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Member-widget sound slot: plays the u16 sound id at actor-record+0xB4 through the shared sound player.
evidence: The body is one Sound_PlaySeById with the u16 at record+0xB4 (record = *(self+0x12D8)), i.e. a sound, not an animation - the previous 'PlayAnimB' wording was wrong. It is vtable slot 1 of the member-animation table 0x0075CDD4, alongside the +0xBE and +0xB6 twins.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberAnim_PlaySeC
signature: void Battle_Ui_MemberAnim_PlaySeC(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Member-widget sound slot: plays the u16 sound id at actor-record+0xBE through the shared sound player.
evidence: Same one-call body as 0x003CB4EC but reading +0xBE, vtable slot 0 of the same 0x0075CDD4 table; the field holds a sound id, so 'PlaySe' replaces the old 'PlayAnim' wording.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_PlaySePair
summary: Plays the two member sounds stored at actor-record+0xB0 and +0xB2 in order, through the shared sound player.
evidence: Two consecutive Sound_PlaySeById calls on +0xB0 and +0xB2, vtable slot 17 of 0x0075CD88; the 'Pair' suffix matches the code exactly.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberAnim_PlaySeD
signature: void Battle_Ui_MemberAnim_PlaySeD(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Member-widget sound slot: plays the u16 sound id at actor-record+0xB6 through the shared sound player.
evidence: Same one-call body as its B/C siblings, reading +0xB6; vtable slot 2 of 0x0075CDD4. Sound id, not animation.

name: maybe_Ui_PageControl_UpdateLayout
summary: Rebuilds the page table of a paged widget: allocates one 0x98-byte UI object per page, drives the two directions of each page's animation controller (vtable +0x44/+0x20) and finally plays SE 0x89.

name: Ui_MessagePanel_HideWithSound

name: Script_ParseBinaryExpression

evidence: The 8-row page arithmetic, the named Ui_List_SelectEntryById / Message_SetArg calls and the table slot 0x0072A3A8 place it in the spell (jumon) window, but the window class itself is unnamed and the same shape appears in the item list, so the 'Jumon' identity rests on the table slot only.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_MoveCursor
summary: Cursor movement on an item screen: handles the left/right and up/down input bits with page-wrap arithmetic (page sizes 11/12), moves the visible list, resolves the member record for the new slot, sets message argument 2 to the member name and commits the selection.
evidence: The page-size constants 0xB/0xC, the named Ui_List_SelectEntryById / Message_SetArg / Item_LookupRecord calls and the member-slot lookup func_0035EB98 are all present, but the screen object comes from func_00311524 which is unnamed, so 'ItemScreen' is inherited from the first pass.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_SelectOffsetItem

summary: Tactics (sakusen) window helper: reads the selected member from the pane at self[0x7B], takes that member's stored offset (f_E4), switches the window to state 0x0C, refreshes the list part at self[0x8D] and asks Ui_List_SelectEntryById to select entry (list first id + offset).
evidence: The named Ui_PartyStatusWindow_GetSelectedMemberId, func_0035EB98 member record and Ui_List_SelectEntryById calls are concrete, as is the state 0x0C push; the sakusen identity comes from the pane-name evidence recorded in the file header (win_sakusen2), which is strong but still one step removed.

name: maybe_Ui_TsuyosaWindow_UpdateRowText
signature: void maybe_Ui_TsuyosaWindow_UpdateRowText(TsuyosaRow* row, int row2, int value, u32 string)
summary: Fills one row of the party-strength (tsuyosa) comparison window: copies the row's pane names ('txt', 'txt_Al0', 'txt_Dl_2_0', ...) into the 12 u16 columns at row+0x54 + line*0x30, selects the list entry, formats the row text and re-applies the row.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemList_ScrollToFirstNonEmpty
summary: Scrolls an item list back to the top and then to the first usable row: resolves the member at self[0x17], counts its entries, walks the slots with func_006292A4 until one qualifies and moves the pager with the divide-by-12 page/row arithmetic used by the equipment list.
evidence: The named Ui_ScrollList_ScrollToTop, func_0035EB98 member record and the 0x2AAAAAAB/12 page math are visible, but the qualification test is func_006292A4 (the equipped-slot check), so 'first non-empty' is only partly right - the list is being positioned on the first *unequipped* slot, and that nuance cannot be confirmed without the caller (0x0019A514 is unnamed).

name: Ui_DiveForm_BuildPageEntries
summary: Fills one page of the dive mini-game form: copies the 0x48-byte page table from 0x0072C570, and for each of the page's entries resolves the pack record (Pack_FindRecordByIndex), sets the pane text, stores the entry id byte at +0x50 and finally sets the animation states for the eight rows and selects the page's first entry.
evidence: The static 0x48-byte page table, the named Pack_FindRecordByIndex and Ui_List_SelectEntryById calls and the per-row animation loop make a page build; the only caller is maybe_Ui_DiveForm_OnPageSelect (0x003D83C0), which confirms the page context.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_EnsureEntrySelected
summary: Small window helper: asks the window to ensure its current entry is visible, then fetches the bound list object through vtable +0x58 and selects the entry encoded in self->f_98 (high half) on it.
evidence: The 28-byte body is Ui_ListWindow_EnsureEntryVisible followed by vtable +0x58 and Ui_List_SelectEntryById with `f_98 << 16` - nothing is detached and no render node appears, so the previous 'DetachRenderNode' name was wrong. The same select-by-id pattern appears at 0x002D888C and 0x00214A78.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_SetDrawPriority
summary: Stores a new value at self+0x2C and, when the object owns a draw object at +0x38, refreshes it (0x001D7EEC) and pushes the value into it through 0x001D809C.
evidence: The store-then-apply shape is clear, but the value is only 'priority' if +0x2C is the draw priority, and 0x001D809C is currently named Ui_List_SelectEntryById even though it is used here (and in the animation-frame helper) as a generic set-value call - the callee name is the weak link.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SelectEntryA
summary: Asks the window for its bound list object (vtable +0x58) and selects the entry id stored at the u16 self+0x28 on it (high-half encoding).

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdateCounter
summary: Odometer-style counter tick of the tactics window: unless the fast-forward flags are set it advances the displayed number, derives the ones digit with a divide-by-ten, clamps it to 9, updates the digit glyph and the composed value and stores the carry in f_8CC; the busy bit only refreshes the message layout.
evidence: The 0x66666667 magic constant (divide by 10), the digit clamp to 9, the carry field f_8CC and the two widget updates are all in the body, and it sits between Ui_SakusenWindow_Update and Ui_SakusenWindow_OnInput, so both the screen and the counter role are supported.

name: maybe_Ui_GridCursor_HandleInput
summary: Input handler for a grid/list cursor: on the cancel bit it pops the pane, on the confirm bits it asks the controller at self+0x420 for the chosen cell (0xFF = none) and commits it, and on the direction bits it computes the next cell with 0x002B1CC8 and binds the index to the cell's draw object.
evidence: The flag word self+0x3770, the controller self+0x420 and the index-binding call are visible, and the object layout is the same as the dive form's (self+0x134 pane stack, self+0x37D4 state), but the two neighbours 0x002B1A9C / 0x003D84DC differ only in which controller getter they call, so which one is 'grid cursor' and which is 'text input' is not decidable from the bodies alone.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_OnTextInput
summary: Text-entry handler of the dive form: on cancel it pops the pane, on confirm/choice bits it reads the typed value from the field at self+0x420, sets the accepted flags (f_3778, state f_10/f_4E) and refreshes the entry object.
evidence: Same object layout and flag word as 0x002B1A9C but with the other controller getter (0x00654058); the handler-table reference 0x0072C4C8 entry 0x0072C510 ties it to the dive form, yet the 'text input' part is still an interpretation of the field write (f_4E = typed char).

name: Ui_MainWindow_SelectListByEventId
summary: Maps a UI event id (1..10) to a list index (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, else 0) and selects that entry in the bound list, using the self->f_1A8 page in the high half of the id.
evidence: The whole switch and the single Ui_List_SelectEntryById call are visible, and the write-0 default covers the 'no mapping' case; the only unknown is what the event ids mean to the caller, which does not affect the name.

name: maybe_Ui_List_SelectById
summary: Asks the window for its bound list object (vtable +0x58) and, when present, selects the entry id stored at the u16 self+0x28 (high-half encoding).
evidence: The identity with 0x00214A78 (same three operations) proves it is a select-by-id helper rather than anything window-specific, but which window owns it and whether +0x28 is really an id is still inferred from the 0x001D809C calling convention.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SelectEntryC
summary: Asks the object for its bound list (vtable +0x58) and selects the entry id stored at the u16 self+0x28 on it (high-half encoding).
evidence: Third copy of the same three-operation body as 0x002D888C and 0x00214A78; nothing here touches a text layout or commits a line, so the previous 'Text_CommitLine' name was wrong. The C suffix marks the third identical copy.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemList_ScrollToIndex
summary: Moves an item list to the page containing the current (last) index: converts the index to page/row with the divide-by-12 magic constant, writes the row position through the list model, stores the page at self[0x13] and clamps the page to the 11/12-row range before applying it.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_AdvanceScrollPage
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_AdvanceScrollPage(Ui_ListWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, int page)
summary: Scroll helper of a list window: forwards to maybe_Ui_ScrollList_ScrollBy, and when the entry count plus the stored page times five reaches the visible-row count it commits the new scroll offset through the window's own vtable and updates the stored page word.

name: Ui_ListWindow_CommitSelection
summary: Commits the list window's current selection: stops the selection animation (vtable +0x5C), fetches the bound list (vtable +0x58) and pushes value combined with the window id in the high half into it.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_UpdateSpeakerName
summary: Refreshes the speaker/actor text of a message window: validates the attached actor against the sentinel list, rebuilds the text rows through maybe_Ui_ScrollBar_BuildRows, resets the scroll counter and re-selects the row in the label object.
evidence: The named maybe_Ui_ScrollBar_BuildRows, the text-label selection and the row clamp are visible, but the function does not obviously write a *name* - it rebuilds the message rows for the attached actor, so 'speaker name' is narrower than the code.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_SelectEntryByCursor

name: maybe_Ui_DiveWindow_ApplySelection

name: Ui_ListWindow_SetSourceList
summary: Points a list window at a new source list: stores the source at self[0x2B], copies the source's entry count into the list model, resets the model to row 0, notifies the owner (vtable +0x6C) and sets or clears the 'has rows' bit on the selected pane.
evidence: The store-then-copy-then-reset sequence with the named maybe_Container_SetCountFromByteSize and maybe_Ui_TextListWindow_UpdateItemRects is a source-list assignment, and the trailing bit-0 update of pane+0x44 is the 'rows present' indicator.

name: maybe_Ui_ChoiceSelectWindow_SelectByRecord
summary: Selects the first usable entry of a choice window: reads the entry-count byte from the attached record (f_198->f_6D), resolves the choice group through the data manager, walks the entries with the validity test 0x00666908 and forwards the first valid index (clamped to 4) to the list widget.
evidence: The named maybe_Data_ValidateGroupSlots and func_00666908 validity walk plus the final list select are visible, and the layout pointer f_198->f_6D is read consistently; the choice-window class itself is unnamed, so the prefix and the clamp purpose are inferred.

name: Ui_ListWindow_SetupRows
summary: Fills the seven visible rows of a list window starting at firstRow: each row takes its 0x8C-byte source record from the table at self->f_AC (bounds-checked against the count at table+0x1CFC), writes the row label through func_001A6680 with the row index packed above the window id, and hands the selected row (firstRow*7+i modulo 7) to the child list control.
evidence: The fixed 7-row loop, the 0x8C source stride, the bounds checks against self->f_4C and table+0x1CFC and the packed label ids are all explicit in the body; the modulo-7 via 0x92492493 confirms seven visible rows.

name: Ui_ListWindow_SelectRow
summary: Selects a row in the list window: resets the selection byte f_2A to 0xFF, resizes the highlight container to the entry count from the source table (+0x1CFC), scrolls so the requested row is visible (row modulo 7) and notifies the window through vtable +0x6C.
evidence: The count read, the named maybe_Container_SetCountFromByteSize / maybe_Ui_TextListWindow_UpdateItemRects calls, the modulo-7 split and the negative-row branch are all visible, matching its sibling Ui_ListWindow_SetupRows.

name: Ui_ListWindow_ScrollByRows
summary: Scrolls a list window by delta rows: adds the current page times ten and the visible-row count, wraps/clamps the result into the row count, selects it through Ui_List_SelectEntryById with the window id in the high half and refreshes the scroll bar through vtable +0x60.
evidence: The count/page/visible arithmetic with the 10-rows-per-page constant and the final refresh are explicit; the name is corrected from 'ScrollToRow' because the function adds the caller's delta to the current page instead of jumping to an absolute row.

name: maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByPageThumbA

name: maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByPageThumbB

name: maybe_Ui_List_ScrollClampRows12
signature: void maybe_Ui_List_ScrollClampRows12(void* list, int (*getCount)(int), u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int cursor, int max)
summary: Thumb scroll clamp for a 12-row list: compares the cursor row against the row count, derives the page with the divide-by-12 magic constant, clamps the scroll offset into the 11/12-row window, re-selects the entry and refreshes the scroll bar.
evidence: The 0x2AAAAAAB divide-by-12 and the 0xB/0xC clamp values are visible, but two of the row values come from unaff_r5/unaff_r6, the function sits in the unreferenced 0x6E5xxx Thumb fragment block and ends in an unrecovered jump table; only the arithmetic shape is trustworthy.

name: maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByPageThumbC
summary: Third Thumb page-scroll fragment of a list window: clamps the target row to the 11/12-row range, sets the scroll position through 0x001A61FC, re-selects the entry and refreshes the window through vtable +0x60.
evidence: Every argument is lost (unaff_r4/r5/r7/r8, arg2/arg5/arg6 undefined), the body calls through an unrecovered jump table and nothing in the image references this address, so it is a fragment of a larger scroll routine rather than a standalone function.

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollGrid_MoveCursor
signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollGrid_MoveCursor(void* self, int delta, u32 arg3, int pageCount)
summary: Grid variant of the list scroll mover: adds the delta to the current row, computes the page as (count-1)/8 and then moves a second linked list (the sibling pane at +1) together with the first using the divide-by-12 sheet arithmetic.
evidence: The `(count-1) >> 3` page computation and the second-list handling are readable, but the body is truncated by halt_baddata three times (delta==0, pageCount==0, row==0) and the caller list (maybe_Ui_PanelGroup_Update, maybe_Ui_Model_UpdateAttachedParts) is generic UI update code, so neither the grid identity nor the two-list role is proven.

signature: void maybe_Ui_List_ScrollByDeltaThumb(void* list, int delta, u32 arg3, int listHandle)
summary: Thumb scroll-by-delta step for a 12-row list window: adds the delta to the stored row, clamps the resulting offset into the 11/12-row window and re-selects and refreshes the list.

name: Ui_EquipmentWindow_SetItemPanesA
summary: Fills the four icon panes of an equipment row: the two fixed slot markers (sprite ids 0x60 and 0x61), then the item icon of the member's equipped item in slot 4 and the secondary icon, falling back to the empty icon when the item has no icon data; sets the 'filled' byte at self+0x49 to 0.
evidence: The member record func_0035EB98, the equipped-item lookup func_006292F0(record,4), Item_LookupRecord and the empty-icon fallback are all named or documented, and both callers (Ui_EquipmentWindow_UseItemLogic and 0x00617FB0) are equipment paths.

name: Ui_EquipmentWindow_SetItemPanesB
summary: Second icon-setter of the equipment row: draws the two compare markers (sprite ids 0x5C/0x5D, swapped when maybe_Item_GetEquipCategory returns 0) and then the item icons read from equipment slots 0 and 1, with the empty-icon fallback; sets the 'filled' byte to 1.
evidence: Same caller pair and pane-key layout as its confirmed sibling Ui_EquipmentWindow_SetItemPanesA, with the 0x5C/0x5D swap driven by the named maybe_Item_GetEquipCategory and the item ids taken from slots 0/1 instead of slot 4.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipmentWindow_SetItemCode
summary: Resolves the current item (an already-prepared item record passed in the caller's stack slot), decodes it with func_0066C2DC and stores the resulting u16 code in the UI manager's shared word at +0x94.
evidence: The Item_LookupRecord + func_0066C2DC + store to uiCore+0x94 is only three operations and the item id comes from an argument the decompiler lost, so 'equipment window' and 'item code' are inherited from the first pass; the UI core word +0x94 is shared with other UI decoders.
